dct_description_sm: "Agency office locations located that service tribes at the reservation level. The twelve regional offices located in the heart of Indian Country. The Bureau of Indian Affairs Central Office oversees all the the regional offices and is also included in this file. Delivery of program services to the federally recognized tribes and individual Indians and Alaska Natives, whether directly or through contracts, grants or compacts, is administered by the 12 regional offices and 83 agencies that report to the BIA Deputy Director-Field Operations, located in Washington, D.C. Each regional office is headed by a Regional Director who is responsible for all Bureau activities within a defined geographical area except education, law enforcement and functions of an administrative nature. The typical Regional Office includes a Deputy Regional Director for Trust Services and Deputy Regional Director for Indian Services. The twelve regional offices are located in the heart of Indian Country with the agencies located at the reservation level. These regional offices services the needs of specific tribes. The Bureau of Indian Affairs Central Office oversees all the the regional offices and is also included in this file"--Metadata XML file.
